bib.title: EvoPrompting: Language Models for Code-Level Neural Architecture Search
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

read.skipped: References skimmed only; code listings in A.2, A.4, A.5 read as code, not line by line; figures not rendered (captions from text).

question: Can a code-pretrained LM, used as an adaptive crossover and mutation operator inside an evolutionary loop with soft prompt-tuning, design better neural architectures than few-shot prompting alone?
hypothesis: Evolving the in-context examples and prompt-tuning the LM between rounds lets an LM find accurate, small architectures that naive few-shot prompting cannot.
contributions: EvoPrompting, evolutionary search that creates and curates data to improve LM in-context prompting examples
A study applying LMs to code-level neural architecture design; few-shot prompting alone is unsuccessful, with EvoPrompting it beats human-expert designs
Novel GNN architectures found with EvoPrompting that beat Triplet-GMPNN on 21 of 30 CLRS tasks

method.summary: A 62B PaLM code model proposes architectures as Python code from 2-shot prompts built from the top-fitness survivors, each child is trained and scored (fitness = -(model size x validation error)), the top 10 become parents, and all other evaluated children prompt-tune the LM for the next round. Run for 10 rounds on MNIST-1D and, over triplet representations, on three CLRS tasks.
method.task: neural architecture search at code level (CNNs on MNIST-1D, GNN triplet representations on CLRS)

datasets.name: MNIST-1D
datasets.split: 500 of the 4000 training examples held out as validation

datasets.name: CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark
datasets.split: search on articulation points, Graham scan and Kruskal MST; OOD accuracy reported on all 30
datasets.preprocessing: followed single-task hyperparameters of Ibarz et al. 2022

datasets.name: NATS-Bench size search space (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-16-120)
datasets.preprocessing: LM prompted to emit architecture strings like 64:64:64:64:64

models.name: PaLM 62B (crossover/mutation operator, pi_theta0)
models.architecture: decoder-only PaLM, additionally fine-tuned on 64B tokens of near-deduplicated permissively licensed GitHub Python
models.init_from: pre-trained on 1.3T tokens of conversational, web and code documents

models.name: MNIST-1D seed models
models.architecture: 4 seeds: GRU, CNN, MLP from Greydanus 2020, plus a larger hand-designed CNN; Flax

models.name: Triplet-GMPNN
models.architecture: message-passing GNN with gating and triplet edge processing; 9 seed variants in Haiku/Jax

training.objective: outer loop: prompt-tuning of the LM on evaluated children (CEVALED minus parents); inner loop: child classifiers trained on the task
training.lr: 0.1 (soft prompt-tuning); 0.01 (MNIST-1D child models); CLRS child lr per Ibarz et al. 2022, not restated
training.steps: 8000 per MNIST-1D child; 2000 per CLRS child
training.hardware: single NVIDIA Tesla P100 GPU per child model

other.children_per_search: 1600 (10 rounds x 10 prompts x 16 samples); duplicates and untrainable still count

inference.samples: n=16 samples per prompt, m=10 prompts per round, 160 children per round
inference.prompting: 2-shot; each example is a docstring with metrics dict (num_params, val_accuracy) then model code; last line gives target metrics: size 90% of min parent size rounded to nearest 100, accuracy 102% of max parent accuracy rounded to nearest 0.1%

parameters.alpha: 0.5 (Table 2 'Lower threshold for test error'; text calls it an upper threshold on validation error)
parameters.parent_selection: top p by fitness in global population; parents are removed and not reused

metrics.name: fitness
metrics.definition: negative product of validation error and model size

metrics.name: test error vs model size (Pareto frontier of top 20)
metrics.definition: MNIST-1D test error against parameter count

metrics.name: OOD accuracy
metrics.definition: CLRS out-of-distribution accuracy of discovered models vs Triplet-GMPNN

baselines: REA, REINFORCE, RANDOM, BOHB and weight-sharing methods on NATS-Bench (numbers from Dong et al. 2021)
eval.protocol: Max-fitness curves estimated with 100 bootstrap samples of size 20; CLRS OOD accuracy as mean +/- error from table; number of search runs not stated

availability.data: MNIST-1D and CLRS public; search code not stated

prompts.where: Listing 1, Section 3.3 (second in-context example omitted in the paper)

results.claim: EvoPrompting finds CLRS GNN triplet representations that beat Triplet-GMPNN on 21 of 30 tasks.
results.quote: outperform current state-of-the-art models on 21 out of 30 algorithmic

results.claim: Heapsort OOD accuracy rises by 125.19% with CONCATREP at only 6.68% more parameters.
results.quote: CONCATREP increased OOD accuracy by 125.19% while only increasing model size by 6.68% over the baseline

results.claim: Heapsort OOD accuracy, CONCATREP vs Ibarz et al. baseline.
results.table: Table 1, row Heapsort, column OOD Accuracy Ours (69.9 +/- 4.2%)
results.note: Table 3 prints 69.90 and 31.04; our own baseline reimplementation scores 19.45 (Table 3)

results.claim: Bubble Sort OOD accuracy with CONCATREP.
results.table: Table 1, row Bubble Sort, column OOD Accuracy Ours (88.9 +/- 2.8%)
Table 1, row DFS, column OOD Accuracy Ours (68.1 +/- 1.4%)

results.claim: Each component matters on MNIST-1D: random-parent EvoPrompting with prompt-tuning is no more effective than naive prompting.
results.setup: MNIST-1D, Fig 2a Pareto frontier of top 20 models
results.quote: prompting with randomly selected parents combined with prompt-tuning is no more effective than naive prompting alone

results.claim: Random-parents baseline plateaus at about 200 generated individuals; full EvoPrompting plateaus highest and latest.
results.quote: reaching a maximum fitness by the time approximately 200 individuals

results.claim: Search budget: 1600 models generated per search.
results.quote: yielding a total of 160 models generated per round and 1600 models generated during the entire search

results.claim: Naive few-shot prompting alone is unsuccessful at NAS; the LM needs evolution plus prompt-tuning.
results.quote: NAS still proves too difficult a task for LMs to succeed at solely through prompting

results.claim: On NATS-Bench CIFAR-10 test accuracy EvoPrompting reaches 93.11, comparable to REA 93.22 but not the best (93.40 channel-wise interpolation).
results.setup: NATS-Bench size space, handicapped setup (string output, no code pretraining)
results.table: Table 4, row EVOPROMPTING, column CIFAR-10 Test

limits: Authors concede no extensive comparison against standard NAS techniques, since EvoPrompting is designed for open-ended search; only one NATS-Bench comparison, itself handicapped (A.7).
Searches on CLRS were run on only 3 tasks; 5 of the discovered models analysed; more variation than on MNIST-1D (Sec 4.2).
Number of independent search runs, seeds and total compute are not stated; code is not stated as released.
Child models trained only 2000 steps on CLRS as a proxy; fitness favours small models and needs an error threshold alpha to prevent gaming.
Text calls alpha an upper threshold, Table 2 calls it a lower threshold; text says validation error is the fitness input but MNIST-1D plots use test error.
On 9 of 30 CLRS tasks the baseline remained best (Table 3).

terms.definition: evolutionary prompt engineering combined with soft prompt-tuning, with the LM as crossover and mutation operator

lineage.note: evolutionary NAS over hand-designed search spaces
